items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: And really when he got with Miles that’s when he really blossomed.

ctx.x: You’ve got quite a list of kids you had as students who have gone on to some great things. That must make you feel pretty good, in addition to your own kids.

Well the thing about that, it’s a double edged sword. The ones that you taught, I don’t take credit for none of them because if I take credit for all them I got to take credit for all them who didn’t do anything. So when you come to it, yeah they passed through, they got whatever they were supposed to get and some of them, believe it or not, some of them were as good as all the rest of them but they just didn’t get the breaks. I know some people that could really play when all of them was on that level. But as…

whole lot of players that went down that didn’t do it. So what I tell people, I can’t take the credit for you and not take the credit for all the rest of them so there’s a lot of them that didn’t make it, but I still love them and at the time they were doing what they were supposed to do. And I can understand why some of them say man look I’m going to do this, I’m going to do this, I’m going to do that, and I’ll play on the weekends and I’m not going to put all my time into this. And you know that’s a part of it,…
